findings.title: A time entry can be saved with an end before its start, producing negative hours and negative pay

evidence.detail: start and end are built independently from separate date and time pickers. Nothing checks end > start before submit (line 52), and the screen shows 'Duration' with a negative value at line 127.
submit() writes the entry to Firestore without any validation, so the negative duration is stored and feeds the per-day and 'All Entries' totals the listing advertises.

fix.recipe: Disable Save and show an inline error when end is not after start. Also reject it in EntryScreenController.submit and add a unit test.

findings.guideline: Android: Minimum functionality; Metadata policy (listing must match behaviour)
findings.title: Hourly rate accepts whole numbers only and invalid input silently becomes 0, so the pay the listing promises disappears

evidence.detail: The rate field has decimal: false (line 125), no validator, and saves int.tryParse(value) ?? 0. An entry like 12.50 or an empty field is stored as rate 0 with no message.
Pay is only displayed when ratePerHour > 0, so a silently dropped rate hides pay everywhere.
The Android description promises seeing 'how much pay each job adds up to'.

fix.recipe: Add a validator that rejects empty or non-numeric rates, or allow decimals and store the rate as a double or integer cents. Show an error instead of defaulting to 0.

findings.guideline: Android: Minimum functionality (crashes and broken experience)
findings.title: Entries tab fails to load when an entry has no matching job, which deleting a job can briefly cause

evidence.detail: jobs.firstWhere(...) has no orElse. An entry whose job is missing throws StateError and the whole combined stream errors, so the Entries tab shows an error instead of the totals.

deleteJob deletes entries one at a time, then the job (line 49), so the two streams can disagree. A failure part-way, such as going offline, leaves permanent orphan entries and the Entries tab stays broken for that account.

fix.recipe: Skip entries whose job is missing in _entriesJobsCombiner. Delete the job and its entries in one Firestore batch. Add a test with an orphaned entry.

findings.guideline: Android: User Data policy (Data safety form must match the privacy policy and actual behaviour)
findings.title: Data safety declares an optional display name that the privacy policy does not mention, and the profile also reads a photo URL

evidence.detail: UserAvatar reads the profile photo URL and EditableUserDisplayName (line 28) lets the user store a display name in the auth profile.
'What we store' lists email, password hash, anonymous ID, jobs and entries, but not the display name or a photo URL.

fix.recipe: Add the optional display name (and photo URL, if it can be set) to the privacy policy so it matches the Data safety form.

findings.guideline: Android: User Data policy (account deletion requirements)
findings.title: Deletion erases the data before the account, and anonymous users may be unable to complete re-authentication

evidence.detail: deleteAllUserData runs before user.delete() (line 58). Any failure other than requires-recent-login, such as a network drop, leaves the account alive with its data gone, and the user sees only a generic error.

The default re-auth dialog uses authProviders, which contains only EmailAuthProvider. An anonymous user, whom review_notes.yaml sends to test deletion, has no credential to re-enter if Firebase asks for a recent sign-in. The cancel path (line 79) tells the user to 'sign in again', which an anonymous user cannot do.

fix.recipe: Re-authenticate (or confirm a recent sign-in) before deleting data. Handle anonymous users explicitly, for example by deleting them directly. Retry the account delete with a clear message on failure.

findings.guideline: Android: App access (reviewer must reach all functionality)
findings.title: Review notes promise a seeded demo account, but nothing in the repo creates or refreshes that data

evidence.detail: Claims the demo account already has two jobs with time entries. Line 7 says it is re-seeded before each submission. No script, fixture or CI job in the repo (only scripts/demo-video and tools/ci) creates the account or its Firestore data.
With an empty account the reviewer sees 'No jobs yet'. Job entries, edit and the Entries day totals only show content after data exists, so an unseeded account fails the Minimum functionality check.

fix.recipe: Create the reviewer account and seed two jobs with entries in the production Firebase project before submitting. Ideally commit an idempotent seed script that CI runs, so the re-seeding claim is true.

findings.title: Release builds show a raw exception dump on a red screen when a widget fails to build

evidence.detail: ErrorWidget.builder (line 38) is set with no kDebugMode guard and renders details.toString() to users. Errors are only debugPrint-ed (lines 30 and 34), so nothing is reported either.

fix.recipe: Show a short friendly message with a retry action in release builds and keep the detail for kDebugMode.
